title.raw: 卷三十一 志第十一: 音樂四 Volume 31 Treatises 11: Music 4

translations.literal: Treatise 11, Music IV
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 11: Music, Part Four

sentences.zh: 享太廟樂章十三首貞觀中魏徵褚亮等作

translations.literal: Thirteen hymn pieces for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, composed in the Zhenguan era by Wei Zheng, Chu Liang, and others
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen hymns for sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, written in the Zhenguan reign by Wei Zheng, Chu Liang, and others

sentences.zh: 迎神用《永和》黃鐘宮三成，大呂角二成，太簇徵二成，應鐘羽二成，總九變同用。

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirits, use "Yonghe"; Huangzhong palace mode three sequences, Dalü horn mode two sequences, Taicu sharp mode two sequences, Yingzhong feather mode two sequences—in all nine modal changes used together.
translations.idiomatic: The reception of the spirits uses "Everlasting Harmony," in Huangzhong gong with three repetitions, Dalü jue with two, Taicu zhi with two, and Yingzhong yu with two—nine modal shifts in all, employed together.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: How majestic is the august ancestor; he enlarged this grand foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic is our honored founder; he spread this great foundation wide.

translations.literal: Ever to accord with Heaven's mandate, may descendants preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: Forever to match Heaven's command—let our heirs guard it always.

translations.literal: The hundred spirits are all attuned; the myriad states rest here.
translations.idiomatic: All spirits are in harmony; every realm finds its place here.

translations.literal: Therefore with filial offerings we present the sacrifice; may the spirits come to us.
translations.idiomatic: Hence we offer this filial rite, that the gods may draw near in grace.

sentences.zh: 皇帝行用《太和》詞同冬至圓丘。

translations.literal: For the emperor's procession, use "Taihe"; the text is the same as for the winter solstice at the Round Mound Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's procession uses "Supreme Harmony," with the same lyrics as at the winter solstice rites on the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 登歌酌鬯用《肅和》夾鐘均之黃鐘羽：

translations.literal: For the ascent hymn with libation of fragrant wine, use "Suhe," in the Huangzhong feather of the Jiazhong key:
translations.idiomatic: The ascent hymn and libation use "Solemn Harmony," in Huangzhong yu under the Jiazhong tonal standard:

translations.literal: Great indeed is the utmost virtue; truly this is enlightened sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: Vast is the supreme virtue; here is true enlightened rule.

translations.literal: Reaching above and below, thereby following sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: It reaches high and low alike, and so we keep to reverent truth.

translations.literal: Joyfully the music rises; sounding pearls to chant praise.
translations.idiomatic: With glad music we ascend, and pearl chimes sing the praise.

translations.literal: May the spirits descend and alight; thereby exalting the bright mandate.
translations.idiomatic: May the gods descend among us and lift high the radiant Mandate.

translations.literal: For welcoming the offering stands, use "Yonghe":
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the sacrificial stands uses "Harmonious Peace":

translations.literal: Exalt this sacrificial service; sincerity and reverence both arrive.
translations.idiomatic: We honor this offering rite with sincerity and reverence complete.

translations.literal: Music thereby moves the spirits; ritual thereby displays the service.
translations.idiomatic: Music moves the divine; ritual makes the service plain.

translations.literal: Grain offerings all pure, sacrificial beasts fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The grain offerings are wholly pure; the victims are fully prepared.

translations.literal: Ever speak of filial thought; perhaps there will be no lack.
translations.idiomatic: Ever hold filial remembrance, that nothing may ever fail.

sentences.zh: 皇祖宣簡公酌獻用《長髮》無射宮：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Imperial Ancestor Duke Xuanjian, use "Changfa," Wushe palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Imperial Ancestor Duke Xuanjian uses "Long Hair," in Wushe gong:

translations.literal: Deep wisdom is Tang's; long hair—its auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Deep wisdom belongs to Tang; long flourishing is its omen.

translations.literal: Heaven's command thus blesses; the royal enterprise can flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate blesses us; the royal work flourishes.

translations.literal: Matching Heaven, bearing virtue; approaching the sun, redoubled radiance.
translations.idiomatic: He matches Heaven and bears virtue; he turns to the sun and doubles its light.

translations.literal: Root and branches for a hundred generations; repeatedly bestowed without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Root and branch for a hundred generations—blessings granted without end.

sentences.zh: 皇祖懿王酌獻用《長髮》同前詞，黃鐘宮。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Imperial Ancestor King Yi, use "Changfa," same text as before, Huangzhong palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Imperial Ancestor King Yi uses "Long Hair," with the same lyrics as before, in Huangzhong gong.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝酌獻用《大基》太簇宮：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Great Ancestor Emperor Jing, use "Daji," Taicu palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Great Ancestor Emperor Jing uses "Great Foundation," in Taicu gong:

translations.literal: How admirable the ancestral enterprise; august is the imperial forebear.
translations.idiomatic: How splendid the ancestral work; glorious is the imperial forerunner.

translations.literal: Overthrowing Shang, virtue deep; enfeoffing Tang, felicity prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: He overthrew Shang with deep virtue; he enfeoffed Tang and prolonged its blessing.

translations.literal: Among the Ji line like Hou Ji; compared to Jin, surpassing Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Among the house of Ji he was as Hou Ji; set beside Jin, he surpassed King Xuan.

translations.literal: He founded our tripod destiny for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He laid the foundation of our dynastic fortune for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 世祖元皇帝酌獻用《大成》姑洗宮：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Dynastic Founder Emperor Yuan, use "Dacheng," Guxian palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Dynastic Founder Emperor Yuan uses "Great Accomplishment," in Guxian gong:

translations.literal: Zhou called him King Ji; Jin praised Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou named him King Ji; Jin honored Emperor Wen.

translations.literal: Bright, bright is the flourishing virtue; solemn, solemn, equal in fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Bright shines his flourishing virtue; solemn and fragrant beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 藏用四履，屈道三分，鏗鏘鐘石，載紀鴻勳。

translations.literal: Hiding his use, treading the four quarters; bending the Way, dividing the three parts; resonant bells and stones record great merit.
translations.idiomatic: He concealed his power yet walked the four quarters; he bent the Way and divided the three realms; bells and stones ring out his great achievements.

sentences.zh: 高祖大武皇帝酌獻用《大明》蕤賓宮：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to High Ancestor Emperor Dawu, use "Daming," Ruibin palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The libation to High Ancestor Emperor Dawu uses "Great Brilliance," in Ruibin gong:

translations.literal: The five eras shift in turn; the three beginnings rise in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The five cosmic cycles turn in succession; the three calendar beginnings rise one after another.

translations.literal: Yao and Shun having passed, Yu and Tang rose vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao and Shun were gone, Yu and Tang rose up in power.

translations.literal: Divine martiality commanded the change of age; spiritual favor was received.
translations.idiomatic: Divine valor ordained a new age; heavenly favor was his to receive.

translations.literal: Gazing at clouds displayed virtue; observing latitude threads announced the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He read the clouds and showed his virtue; he watched the heavens and knew the time to march.

translations.literal: Above he bound the celestial warp; below he secured the earth's axis.
translations.idiomatic: Above he bound the fabric of Heaven; below he steadied the pivot of Earth.

translations.literal: He led the army at Zhuoye; the myriad states all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned at Zhuoye, and every state bowed in submission.

translations.literal: He stilled weapons at the Spirit Terrace; the nine officers were truly harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He laid weapons by at the Spirit Terrace; the nine ministers stood in true harmony.

translations.literal: Distant regions submitted in allegiance; cherishing life, they received blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Far lands submitted in allegiance; all living things received his blessing.

translations.literal: Great ritual was already adorned; great music was already harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Great ritual was fully arrayed; great music was brought into harmony.

translations.literal: Black-marked creatures stirred in the parks; red characters floated on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Dark-patterned beasts moved in the royal parks; red writing floated on the river.

translations.literal: Merit proclaimed in the historical records; virtue spread in songs of praise.
translations.idiomatic: His merit fills the chronicles; his virtue lives in songs of praise.

translations.literal: He could make his posterity flourish; a hundred blessings were borne.
translations.idiomatic: He made his descendants flourish; a hundred blessings were theirs to bear.

translations.literal: For the emperor's drinking of blessing, use "Shouhe":
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reception of blessing uses "Longevity and Harmony":

translations.literal: The eight sounds are thus performed; the three offerings are fully presented.
translations.idiomatic: The eight tones sound forth; the three offerings are fully set out.

translations.literal: The precious throne is forever; radiant light renews day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred throne endures forever; its radiance grows new each day.

sentences.zh: 送文舞出迎武舞入用《舒和》：

translations.literal: For sending out the civil dance and welcoming in the martial dance, use "Shuhe":
translations.idiomatic: As the civil dance departs and the martial dance enters, they use "Easy Harmony":

sentences.zh: 聖敬通神光七廟，靈心薦祚和萬方。

translations.literal: Sacred reverence reaches the spirits and illumines the seven temples; the numinous heart offers blessing and harmonizes the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred reverence reaches the gods and lights the seven shrines; a spirit heart offers blessing and brings the world into harmony.

sentences.zh: 嚴禋克配鴻基遠，明德惟馨鳳曆昌。

translations.literal: Solemn sacrifice can match the far-reaching great foundation; bright virtue alone is fragrant—the phoenix calendar flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn rites match a foundation vast and far; bright virtue alone is fragrant—the imperial age flourishes.

sentences.zh: 武舞用《凱安》詞同冬至圓丘。

translations.literal: The martial dance uses "Kaian"; the text is the same as for the winter solstice at the Round Mound Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance uses "Triumphant Peace," with the same lyrics as at the winter solstice on the Round Mound.

translations.literal: For removing the offering stands, use "Yonghe":
translations.idiomatic: Removing the sacrificial stands uses "Harmonious Peace":

translations.literal: How solemn the pure temple; thereby restoring the strict sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is the pure temple; we renew the solemn rite.

translations.literal: The four suspended ensembles are set forth; the three offerings thus cease.
translations.idiomatic: The four ensembles are arrayed; the three offerings come to their close.

translations.literal: The baskets and stands are withdrawn from presentation; humans and spirits receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The vessels are withdrawn from offering; mortals and gods receive blessing.

translations.literal: The spirits alone come to us; bestowing blessing without end.
translations.idiomatic: The gods draw near; they grant blessing without end.

translations.literal: For sending off the spirits, use "Yonghe":
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the spirits uses "Everlasting Harmony":

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn is the pure sacrifice; ascending, ascending is filial thought.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is the pure offering; rising ever is filial remembrance.

translations.literal: Offerings and sacrifices clearly complete; reverent respect is here.
translations.idiomatic: The offerings are fully prepared; reverent devotion is here.

translations.literal: Harmonious song withdraws the stands; prayers of blessing present their words.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious song marks the withdrawal of the stands; prayers of blessing speak their words.

translations.literal: Employing the martial ambition, forever securing the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: May martial purpose shine forth and the great foundation stand forever firm.

sentences.zh: 又享太廟樂章五首永徽已後續撰，不詳撰者。

translations.literal: Also five hymn pieces for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, continued and composed after Yonghui; the composers are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Five further hymns for the Imperial Ancestral Temple, composed after the Yonghui era; the authors are unknown.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝酌獻用《崇德》夷則宮，永徽元年造。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Emperor Taizong Wen, use "Chongde," Yize palace mode, composed in the first year of Yonghui.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Emperor Taizong Wen uses "Honoring Virtue," in Yize gong, composed in Yonghui year 1.

translations.literal: The five cycles changed their divination; a thousand ages opened the sage.
translations.idiomatic: The five cosmic cycles shifted their signs; after a thousand years the sage appeared.

translations.literal: Red clouds gather at dawn; the yellow star shines by night.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson clouds gather at dawn; the yellow star gleams by night.

translations.literal: The era unfolds the pearl satchel; the foundation opens the jade mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The age unfolds its pearl satchel; the foundation opens the jade mirror.

translations.literal: Afterward the chart was opened.
translations.idiomatic: Then the imperial design was unveiled.

translations.literal: Below he overlooks the myriad realms; above he aligns with the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: Below he looks upon the myriad realms; above he aligns with the seven luminaries.

translations.literal: Mist opens the three images; dust is cleared from the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: Mist clears from the three realms; dust is swept from the nine provinces.

translations.literal: The sea is tranquil, stars shine; the distant are at peace, the near are reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Seas are calm and stars shine bright; the far are at peace, the near stand in awe.

translations.literal: Heaven and earth interchange in great peace; Chinese and barbarians gather in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth meet in peace; Chinese and foreign peoples live in harmony.

translations.literal: Flying and swimming return to benevolence; within and without receive secure blessing.
translations.idiomatic: All that fly and swim return to humaneness; within and beyond receive secure blessing.

translations.literal: Achievements surpass deposing Xia; merit is higher than overthrowing Shang.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements surpass the deposition of Xia; his merit exceeds the overthrow of Shang.

translations.literal: Martial displays present the "Seven Virtues"; punishments establish the three chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In war he displayed the Seven Virtues; in law he set forth the three chapters.

translations.literal: Auspicious birds nest in the tower; benevolent beasts roam the beam.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious birds nest in the palace towers; benevolent beasts roam the halls.

translations.literal: Divined years are forever; splendid blessing without bound.
translations.idiomatic: The years foretold are everlasting; splendid blessing knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝酌獻用《鈞天》黃鐘宮，光宅元年造。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang, use "Juntian," Huangzhong palace mode, composed in the first year of Guangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang uses "Harmony of Heaven," in Huangzhong gong, composed in Guangzhai year 1.

translations.literal: Receiving the tally, gathering sagacity to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He received the mandate and gathered sage virtue to ascend the throne.

translations.literal: Far and near cleared, the myriad realms; looking up, harmonizing with the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad realms were cleared far and near; he looked up and aligned with sun, moon, and stars.

translations.literal: Merit accomplished, daily employed; the Way crosses over, the age is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was put to daily use; his Way brought the age to peace.

translations.literal: The jade chart is carried forever; the precious calendar thus flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: The jade chart endures forever; the sacred calendar flourishes.

translations.literal: Sun and moon raise their radiance; mist and clouds blaze in color.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon lift their radiance; mist and clouds blaze with color.

translations.literal: Rivers and mountains present tribute; spirits and earthly powers perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and mountains brought tribute; gods and spirits performed their offices.

translations.literal: Shun's wind thereby lies down; Yao's dawn first arrives.
translations.idiomatic: The wind of Shun lay still at his command; the dawn of Yao came before its time.

translations.literal: Sagely feeling penetrates the realm; filial thought saturates the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Sagely feeling reached through the world; filial thought filled the universe.

translations.literal: Upholding and spreading the ancestors' virtue; reverently following the former hunts.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld the virtue of his forebears and reverently followed their ancient hunts.

translations.literal: Displaying righteousness at heaven's gate; flying blossoms on cloud peaks.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed righteousness at heaven's gate; blossoms flew on cloud-wreathed peaks.

translations.literal: Transformation surpassed the king's standard; spirit concentrated on the imperial forebear.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming power surpassed the royal model; his spirit focused on the imperial ancestor.

translations.literal: Riding clouds, weary of the mundane; driving the sun, ascending to the dark sublime.
translations.idiomatic: He rode the clouds, leaving the world behind; he drove the sun and ascended to the sublime.

sentences.zh: 中宗孝和皇帝酌獻用《太和》太簇宮，景雲元年造。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Emperor Zhongzong Xiaohe, use "Taihe," Taicu palace mode, composed in the first year of Jingyun.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Emperor Zhongzong Xiaohe uses "Supreme Harmony," in Taicu gong, composed in Jingyun year 1.

translations.literal: Broad music is already prepared; fine offerings are already renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand music is fully prepared; fine offerings are freshly set forth.

translations.literal: Narrating the forebears is only virtue; filial offerings are only to kin.
translations.idiomatic: To tell of the ancestors is virtue alone; filial sacrifice is kin alone.

translations.literal: Seven offerings are all raised; five clarified wines are fully presented.
translations.idiomatic: Seven offerings are fully presented; five clarified wines are set out complete.

translations.literal: Bestow this throne-blessing for ten thousand springs.
translations.idiomatic: Grant this throne and blessing for ten thousand springs.

sentences.zh: 睿宗大聖真皇帝酌獻用《景雲》黃鐘宮，開元四年造。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Emperor Ruizong Dasheng Zhen, use "Jingyun," Huangzhong palace mode, composed in the fourth year of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Emperor Ruizong Dasheng Zhen uses "Auspicious Clouds," in Huangzhong gong, composed in Kaiyuan year 4.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: Only the wise becomes a sage; only the sage ascends to emperorship.
translations.idiomatic: Through wisdom he became sage; through sagehood he ascended the throne.

translations.literal: Spiritual essence moves the Radiant Soul; timely receiving flourishing prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: His refined spirit stirred heaven's light; his age rose in bright fortune.

translations.literal: Shun would feel shame before this great filial piety; Yao would yield the throne as king.
translations.idiomatic: Even Shun would blush at such filial virtue; even Yao would defer his crown.

translations.literal: His capability in service reached this utmost; since antiquity, who could match him?
translations.idiomatic: He fulfilled every duty to the height; in all ages, who could equal him?

translations.literal: Civil brilliance treads the wheel of fate; chariots and script share one track.
translations.idiomatic: His enlightened reign held its course; chariots and writing ran on a single way.

translations.literal: Lofty, resplendent—all good, all perfect.
translations.idiomatic: Majestic and radiant, utterly good and complete in beauty.

translations.literal: In the Open Hall the crown's beads hang still; in the Grand Court he sits upright before the screen.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall of audience the crown beads hung quiet; in the great court he sat straight at the screen.

translations.literal: The trust of laying down the burden; the deed gloriously restored the son.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the weight, then laid it down; his act brightly restored his heir.

translations.literal: Casting off shoes in high heaven; ascending to the distant upper realm.
translations.idiomatic: Light as slipping off sandals, he rose from earth to the heavens above.

translations.literal: Dragon Lake, remote and fleeting; elephant fields, lush and unending.
translations.idiomatic: Remote Dragon Lake stretches away; the burial plain rolls on in green.

translations.literal: Procession robes on the elevated way; offering fruits in the first year.
translations.idiomatic: Robe-clad processions on the raised walk; first-year offerings of fruit are set out.

translations.literal: The new temple shines bright; luminous virtue matches Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The new shrine gleams in splendor; his shining virtue stands with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 皇祖宣皇帝酌獻用《光大》無射宮，舊樂章宣、光二宮同用《長髮》，其詞亦同。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to Imperial Ancestor Emperor Xuan, use "Guangda," Wushe palace mode; formerly the Xuan and Guang halls both used "Changfa," with the same text as well.
translations.idiomatic: The libation to Imperial Ancestor Emperor Xuan uses "Great Radiance" in Wushe gong; formerly the Xuan and Guang halls shared "Long Tresses," with identical lyrics throughout.

sentences.zh: 開元十年，始定宣皇帝用《光大》，詞更別造。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaiyuan, it was first fixed that Emperor Xuan would use "Guangda," with separately newly composed lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 10, Emperor Xuan was assigned "Great Radiance," with entirely new lyrics written.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: Great enterprise, dragon blessings; fine repute, swift exaltation.
translations.idiomatic: Great was his work, dragon-blessed; honored name, swiftly exalted.

translations.literal: Dwelling in obscurity, imperial virtue; brilliantly succeeding heaven's kin.
translations.idiomatic: In quiet life he held imperial virtue; his radiance continued Heaven's line.

translations.literal: Displaying rites to the ancestral lords; the filial descendants' sincerity runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Before the forebears the rites unfold; filial heirs bring their weight of truth.

translations.literal: Spring and autumn without end; sacrificial music forever enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Through endless seasons the rites go on; offering and song ever abide.

sentences.zh: 又亨太廟樂章三首太樂舊有此詞，不詳所起。

translations.literal: Also, three hymn pieces for the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Court of Sacral Music long had these lyrics, their origin unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Also three hymns for the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Court Music Bureau preserved these lyrics from old, though their authorship is unknown.

sentences.zh: 迎神黃鐘宮、太呂角、太簇徵、應鐘羽，並同此詞。

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirits: Huangzhong palace, Dalü horn, Taicu sharp, Yingzhong feather—all use this same text.
translations.idiomatic: The reception of the spirits, in Huangzhong gong, Dalü jue, Taicu zhi, and Yingzhong yu, all share these same lyrics.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: The seven temples observe virtue; the hundred spirits all look up.
translations.idiomatic: In seven temples virtue is displayed; all spirits look up in awe.

translations.literal: The customs bear the completion of wealth; creatures are nourished and sustained.
translations.idiomatic: The people receive his shaping hand; all things are fed and kept.

translations.literal: The Way's brilliance holds the covenant; transformation enfolds and lifts the image.
translations.idiomatic: The Way's light upholds the bond; his transforming rule raised the realm's pattern.

translations.literal: Solemn, harmonious—may the spirits come and enjoy the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn and harmonious—may the spirits come to the feast.

translations.literal: Metal performance in Wushe palace mode; next, welcoming the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Metal music in Wushe gong, followed by the reception of the spirits.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn—the clear temple; lofty, lofty—flourishing Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn the clear temple; glorious the thriving Tang.

translations.literal: Paired with Heaven, establishing the pole; accumulated sages, doubled light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's partner, pillar of the realm; sage piled on sage, light on light.

translations.literal: Music harmonizes pipes and chimes; rites complete the steaming sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes and stones in harmony; rites complete with steamed offerings.

translations.literal: Forever may they come; descending blessings without boundary.
translations.idiomatic: May they always draw near; blessings descend without end.

translations.literal: Sending off the spirits:
translations.idiomatic: Spirit departure:

translations.literal: The five sounds are fully performed; the three offerings conclude the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: All five tones sound out; the threefold offering draws to its close.

translations.literal: The carriage moves the phoenix palanquin; banners turn the crimson flags.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix carriage moves away; crimson banners wheel and turn.

translations.literal: The rites complete the vessels; sincerity expresses devout awe.
translations.idiomatic: Every vessel stands complete; sincere awe fills the rite.

translations.literal: The imperial spirits shift the halt; courtiers in official dress bow in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: The royal spirit guards depart; officials bow their leave.

sentences.zh: 則天皇后享清廟樂章十首

translations.literal: Ten hymn pieces for sacrifices at the Clear Temple by Empress Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: Ten hymns for Empress Wu Zetian's sacrifices at the Clear Temple.

translations.literal: First piece:
translations.idiomatic: First hymn:

translations.literal: Establish the clear temple; praise the dark merit.
translations.idiomatic: We raise the clear temple; we praise the hidden work.

translations.literal: Choose an auspicious day; unfold the sacrificial rites to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: A lucky day is chosen; ancestral rites are opened.

translations.literal: The music has already changed; the rites are now exalted.
translations.idiomatic: The music shifts; the rites rise higher still.

translations.literal: Gazing at the spirit carriage; descending to the immortal palace.
translations.idiomatic: We watch for the spirit's coming; it descends to the sacred hall.

translations.literal: Second piece:
translations.idiomatic: Second hymn:

translations.literal: The grand Zhou founded its enterprise; the precious mandate is anew.
translations.idiomatic: The great Zhou laid its founding work; Heaven's mandate was made new.

translations.literal: Revering the ancestors' flourishing canon; thereby displaying devout sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the grand rite, we show our reverent worship.

translations.literal: Sound and brilliance are already prepared; cultural artifacts are now displayed.
translations.idiomatic: With pomp and ceremony complete, ritual objects stand arrayed.

translations.literal: Solemn countenance as if present; earnest will now declared.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn as if they were present; earnest purpose now declared.

translations.literal: Third piece, ascent hymn:
translations.idiomatic: Third hymn, ascent song:

translations.literal: Solemnly spreading the great rite; ascending to pay respects to the honored spirits.
translations.idiomatic: With solemn ceremony we approach the honored spirits on high.

translations.literal: Reverently setting forth basket and silks; bearing crimson sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Basket and silks we reverently set forth, bearing crimson-hearted truth.

translations.literal: Fourth piece, welcoming the spirits:
translations.idiomatic: Fourth hymn, reception of spirits:

translations.literal: Reverently offering water plants; fully expressing the devout heart.
translations.idiomatic: We reverently offer sacred plants; devotion fills our hearts.

translations.literal: Pure sincerity now displayed; awaiting the spirits' descent and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Pure sincerity is shown; we await the spirits' glad descent.

translations.literal: Fifth piece, receiving blessing:
translations.idiomatic: Fifth hymn, drinking the blessing:

translations.literal: There set forth jade wine; thereby setting crimson broth.
translations.idiomatic: Jade wine we set before them; fair libation we pour.

translations.literal: The spirits' hearts have solemnity; assisting blessings without boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits receive in solemn grace; blessings boundless follow on.

translations.literal: Sixth piece, sending off the civil dance:
translations.idiomatic: Sixth hymn, civil dance exit:

translations.literal: The imperial plan grass-cutting and founding; the royal enterprise first opened.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial design was first laid; the royal work newly begun.

translations.literal: Merit high in assisting the mandate; enterprise praising cloud and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: High merit aided Heaven's charge; his work matched the thundercloud's power.

translations.literal: Seventh piece, welcoming the martial dance:
translations.idiomatic: Seventh hymn, martial dance entrance:

sentences.zh: 赫赫玄功被穹壤，皇皇至德洽生靈。

translations.literal: Resplendent, resplendent—dark merit covers heaven and earth; imperial, imperial—utmost virtue moistens living spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His dark merit covered heaven and earth; his supreme virtue warmed every living soul.

sentences.zh: 開基撥亂祅氛廓，佐命宣威海內清。

translations.literal: Opening the foundation, pacifying disorder—the demonic mists cleared; assisting the mandate, proclaiming awe—the realm within the seas is clear.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the realm and cleared turmoil; aided Heaven's charge till the realm was calm within the seas.

translations.literal: Eighth piece, martial dance performance:
translations.idiomatic: Eighth hymn, martial dance:

sentences.zh: 荷恩承顧托，執契恭臨撫。

translations.literal: Bearing grace, accepting the trust-entrustment; holding the covenant, reverently presiding and comforting.
translations.idiomatic: He received grace and trust; holding Heaven's token, he ruled with reverent care.

sentences.zh: 廟略靜邊荒，天兵耀神武。

translations.literal: Temple strategy stills the border wilds; heaven's troops display divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: His strategy stilled the frontier wastes; imperial armies showed divine might.

translations.literal: Ninth piece, removal of the offering trays:
translations.idiomatic: Ninth hymn, clearing the stands:

translations.literal: The ascent hymn has already ended; the offering rites are just completed.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent song has ceased; the offering round is complete.

translations.literal: Reverently receiving bright blessing; solemnly receiving vast favor.
translations.idiomatic: Humbly we receive bright blessing; in awe we accept vast grace.

translations.literal: Tenth piece, sending off the spirits:
translations.idiomatic: Tenth hymn, spirit departure:

translations.literal: The great rite's words are finished; the immortal guards are about to return.
translations.idiomatic: The great rite has run its course; the spirit guard prepares to depart.

translations.literal: Unable to declare crimson earnestness; empty gazing at the Purple Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Words fail our deepest plea; we can only gaze toward the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 中宗孝和皇帝神龍元年享太廟樂章二十首不詳所撰

translations.literal: Twenty hymn pieces for sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple in the first year of Shenlong of Emperor Zhongzong Xiaohe; author unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty hymns for Emperor Zhongzong's Shenlong year 1 sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; authorship unknown.

sentences.zh: 迎神用《嚴和》黃鐘宮三成，大呂角三成，太簇徵三成，應鐘羽二成，同用此詞。

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirits, use "Yanhe"; Huangzhong palace mode three sequences, Dalü horn mode three sequences, Taicu sharp mode three sequences, Yingzhong feather mode two sequences—all use this same text.
translations.idiomatic: The reception of spirits uses "Solemn Harmony"—Huangzhong gong three times, Dalü jue three, Taicu zhi three, Yingzhong yu twice—all with these lyrics.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn—the clear temple; resplendent, resplendent—the dark plans.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn the clear temple; glorious the hidden design.

translations.literal: Merit high through ten thousand ages; transformation covers ten isles.
translations.idiomatic: Merit towering through the ages; transformation reaching every isle.

translations.literal: Central revival of the great enterprise; above receiving Heaven's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration raised a great work; above, Heaven's favor was received.

translations.literal: Only reverently serving the former establishment; rites covering gentle submission.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently we serve the past foundation; rites extend gentle care.

translations.literal: For the emperor's procession, use "Shenghe," Huangzhong palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's procession uses "Ascending Harmony," in Huangzhong gong:

translations.literal: Looking back on my insubstantiality; inheriting the calendar matching the period.
translations.idiomatic: Humble am I to take the throne; I inherit the age Heaven set.

translations.literal: Within and without share the same track; barbarians come to think.
translations.idiomatic: Within and beyond, one path; distant tribes come in devotion.

translations.literal: Music uses exalting virtue; rites thereby set forth words.
translations.idiomatic: Music exalts virtue; rites give voice to prayer.

translations.literal: Evening fear as if in danger; reverently serving the great foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day I stand in caution; reverently I guard the great foundation.

sentences.zh: 登歌稞鬯用《虔和》大呂均之無射羽：

translations.literal: For the ascent hymn with fragrant sacrificial wine, use "Qianhe," in the Wushe feather of the Dalü key:
translations.idiomatic: The ascent hymn and sacrificial wine use "Reverent Harmony," in Wushe yu under the Dalü tonal standard:

translations.literal: The rites mark the recommended fragrant wine; solemn affairs in the ancestral temple court.
translations.idiomatic: The rite marks fragrant wine offered; solemn is the temple court.

translations.literal: Reverently declaring as if present; daring to entrust what is not fragrant enough.
translations.idiomatic: We declare our reverence as if they were here; our poor offering scarcely seems worthy.

sentences.zh: 送文舞出迎武舞入用《同和》太簇羽：

translations.literal: For sending off the civil dance and welcoming the martial dance entering, use "Tonghe," Taicu feather mode:
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance exits and the martial dance enters to "Shared Harmony," in Taicu yu:

sentences.zh: 惟聖配天敷盛禮，惟天為大闡洪名。

translations.literal: Only the sage paired with Heaven spreads the great rite; only Heaven as great opens the vast name.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's peer spreads the great rite; Heaven's greatness opens the honored name.

sentences.zh: 恭禋展敬光先德，萍藻申虔表志誠。

translations.literal: Reverent sacrificial rites display respect to illuminate former virtue; duckweed and altar grass declare sincerity to express will and truth.
translations.idiomatic: With reverent worship we honor our forebears; humble plants express our honest will.

translations.literal: For the martial dance, use "Ninghe," Linzhong sharp mode:
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance uses "Tranquil Harmony," in Linzhong zhi:

sentences.zh: 炎馭失天綱，土德承天命。

translations.literal: The flame chariot lost heaven's net; earth virtue received Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The fiery dynasty lost heaven's rule; earth's virtue received the mandate anew.

sentences.zh: 英猷被寰宇，懿躅隆邦政。

translations.literal: Heroic plans cover the realm; splendid steps uplift state governance.
translations.idiomatic: His heroic design covered all lands; his grand stride lifted the realm's rule.

sentences.zh: 七德已綏邊，九夷鹹底定。

translations.literal: The seven virtues already pacified the borders; the nine barbarians all settled.
translations.idiomatic: Seven martial virtues stilled the frontier; every barbarian land was settled.

sentences.zh: 景化覃遐邇，深仁洽翔泳。

translations.literal: Brilliant transformation extends far and near; deep benevolence moistens flying and swimming.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming light reached far and near; deep kindness warmed all who move and breathe.

sentences.zh: 徹俎用《恭和》大呂均之無射羽：

translations.literal: For removal of the offering trays, use "Gonghe," in the Wushe feather of the Dalü key:
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the stands uses "Reverent Harmony," in Wushe yu under the Dalü tonal standard:

translations.literal: The rites complete the three offerings; the music ends the ninefold completion.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings are fully done; the ninefold music has ended.

translations.literal: Solemnly receiving the spirits' blessings; fearful and cautious, ever filling.
translations.idiomatic: Solemnly we take the spirits' blessing; trembling, our hearts overflow.

translations.literal: For sending off the spirits, use "Tonghe," Huangzhong palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the spirits uses "Universal Harmony," in Huangzhong gong:

translations.literal: The sacrifice's appearance is already complete; the immortal seat thereupon rises.
translations.idiomatic: The rite is finished; the sacred presence rises away.

translations.literal: Slowly, slowly the phoenix rises; misty, misty the clouds ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Gently the phoenix lifts away; softly the clouds rise on high.

translations.literal: Long may the precious fortune flourish; eternally bestow auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: May the imperial fortune long endure; may blessed omens be granted forever.

translations.literal: Blessings extend to posterity; grace covers the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings reach our heirs; favor spreads over all the people.

sentences.zh: 皇后助享、皇后行用《正和》黃鐘宮，詞同貞觀中宮朝會《正和》：

translations.literal: For the empress assisting at the offering and for the empress's procession, use "Zhenghe," Huangzhong palace mode; the text is the same as "Zhenghe" for palace assembly in the Zhenguan era:
translations.idiomatic: When the empress assists at the offering and when she proceeds, "Correct Harmony" is used in Huangzhong gong; the lyrics match the Zhenguan-era "Correct Harmony" for palace assembly:

sentences.zh: 登歌奠鬯用《昭和》大呂均之無射羽８

translations.literal: For the ascent hymn with offering of fragrant wine, use "Zhaohua," Wushe feather under the Dalü tonal standard.
translations.idiomatic: The ascent hymn and libation of fragrant wine use "Bright Harmony," in Wushe yu under the Dalü key.

sentences.zh: 道洽二儀交泰，時休四宇和平。

translations.literal: The Way harmonizes the two principles and brings great peace; the age rests and the four quarters are at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Way joins heaven and earth in harmony; the times are tranquil and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 環佩肅於庭實，鐘石揚乎頌聲。

translations.literal: Jade pendants are solemn among the courtyard offerings; bells and stones raise the hymn of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Pendant jades hang solemn over the offerings in the court; bells and chimes lift the song of praise.

sentences.zh: 皇后酌獻飲福用《誠敬》黃鐘宮：

translations.literal: For the empress's libation offering and drinking the blessing, use "Chengjing," Huangzhong palace mode:
translations.idiomatic: The empress's libation, offering, and blessing wine use "Sincere Reverence," in Huangzhong gong:

translations.literal: Reflecting on my humble substance, I unworthily occupy the pepper palace.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing my humble worth, I unworthily hold the empress's place.

translations.literal: Devoutly offering duckweed and water-cress; solemnly serving the divine ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: With devotion I present the sacred greens; with reverence I serve the royal forebears.

translations.literal: I dare express sincere purity, hoping to exhaust my inmost feelings.
translations.idiomatic: I offer what purity I can, that my deepest heart may be fully shown.

translations.literal: Benevolent countenance is ample; the spirits' enjoyment is without end.
translations.idiomatic: May their gracious presence abound; may the gods feast without end.

sentences.zh: 徹俎用《肅和》大呂均之無射羽：

translations.literal: For removal of the offering trays, use "Suhe," Wushe feather under the Dalü tonal standard:
translations.idiomatic: Clearing the stands uses "Solemn Harmony," in Wushe yu under the Dalü key:

translations.literal: The monthly rites are already complete; "Yunhe" will change.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly service is finished; the music of "Cloud Harmony" shifts away.

translations.literal: Thereupon offering the sacrificial wine; then moving the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Now the spiced wine is offered; now the stands are carried away.

translations.literal: Bright virtue grows ever loftier; though not fragrant, this is what we recommend.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue shines ever brighter; it is not scent alone that we present.

translations.literal: Grace reaches moving and rooted beings; benevolence extends over all the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing touches all that live and grow; kindness spreads through every land.

translations.literal: For sending off the spirits, use "Zhaogan," Huangzhong feather mode:
translations.idiomatic: Sending off the spirits uses "Bright Gratitude," in Huangzhong yu:

translations.literal: Resounding are "Shao" and "Huo"; solemn and reverent is the spirits' countenance.
translations.idiomatic: "Shao" and "Huo" ring out; the gods' presence is grave and still.

translations.literal: Great norms are brilliant; sacrificial rites are harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Grand rule shines forth; the temple rite flows in harmony.

translations.literal: Already completed are the three offerings; about to ride the six dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Three offerings are fully done; the six dragons will soon bear them away.

translations.literal: Sincerity has something to rely on; earnest will has no way to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Our faith was heard, yet our longing cannot follow where they go.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元七年享太廟樂章十六首特進、行尚書左丞相燕國公張說作

translations.literal: Sixteen hymn pieces for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple in the seventh year of Kaiyuan of Emperor Xuanzong, composed by Zhang Yue, Special Advancement, Acting Left Grand Secretary of the Ministry of Revenue, Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen hymns for the Kaiyuan seventh-year offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, written by Zhang Yue, Special Advancement Holder and Acting Left Grand Secretary, Duke of Yan.

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirits, use "Yonghe," three sequences:
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the spirits uses "Everlasting Harmony," in three parts:

translations.literal: Solemn in the nine chambers; harmonizing the eight tones.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence fills the nine halls; the eight sounds fall into harmony.

translations.literal: Sing the emperor's longing; moving the spirits' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We sing the Son of Heaven's yearning and stir the gods' hearts.

translations.literal: Rituals set overnight; music finely explored.
translations.idiomatic: The rites were laid out overnight; the music seeks its subtle depth.

translations.literal: Sounds and brightness complete; fragrant libation arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Sound and splendor are complete; the fragrant offering draws near.

translations.literal: Pitch receives the qi; sound enters the mysterious.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch meets the season's breath; the tone enters the hidden realm.

translations.literal: Leaning on the jade armrest; presiding at the embroidered banquet.
translations.idiomatic: He rests upon the jade armrest and presides at the brocade feast.

translations.literal: Listening to the sighs cease; indistinctly circling.
translations.idiomatic: We listen till the breath falls still; dimly they move and turn.

translations.literal: "Jiushao" throughout; hundred blessings transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: "Nine Shao" is played in full; a hundred blessings pass down.

translations.literal: Trusting the artisans' invocations; eternally praising with sound.
translations.idiomatic: We trust the ritual officers' prayers and forever lift them in song.

translations.literal: Ancestors and forbears come; listening to harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Forefathers draw near and hear the peace of the rite.

translations.literal: Ministering to the hundred lords; tribute from the nine seas.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred ministers attend; the nine seas bring their tribute.

translations.literal: The spirits' blessings are bestowed; the emperor's filiality is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Divine favor is granted; the emperor's filial duty is fulfilled.

translations.literal: For the emperor's procession, use "Taihe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's procession uses "Supreme Harmony," in one part:

translations.literal: The age's cultural sage successor; the pure temple solemn and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Heir to the age's culture and sagehood, he enters the pure temple in solemn grace.

translations.literal: Extending sincerity in diligent offering; in appearance thinking reverence.
translations.idiomatic: With earnest devotion he makes the offering; in bearing he keeps to reverence.

translations.literal: Jade regalia with "Sixia"; golden clang of five bells.
translations.idiomatic: Jade insignia marks "Sixia"; five bells ring out in gold.

translations.literal: Long unbroken cloud-like steps; solemn celestial countenance.
translations.idiomatic: His steps flow on like clouds; his face is grave as heaven.

translations.literal: For the ascent hymn with libation from the jade cup, use "Suhe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The ascent hymn and jade-cup libation use "Solemn Harmony," in one part:

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven filially offers; artisans sing "Pujiang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor offers in filial rite; the singers perform "Broadly We Advance."

translations.literal: Personally performing libation with fragrant sacrificial wine; then burning fat and aromatic herbs.
translations.idiomatic: He himself pours the fragrant wine; then fat and sweet herbs are burned.

translations.literal: Aroma to reach the meaning; sound to seek the yang.
translations.idiomatic: Scent carries the intent upward; music calls the yang force down.

translations.literal: Observing seasonal offerings of winter and autumn; never forgotten through generations.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps the seasonal rites of winter and autumn; never shall they be forgotten.

translations.literal: For welcoming the offering stands, use "Yonghe," two sequences:
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the sacrificial stands uses "Harmonious Peace," in two parts:

translations.literal: At the washing, fine grain-fed beasts; at the stone slab, reverent victims.
translations.idiomatic: At the cleansing stand fine-fed victims; at the binding stone the offerings are made with reverence.

translations.literal: Horn-gripped stallion; solid-colored red bull.
translations.idiomatic: A stallion with firm horns in hand; a pure red bull without blemish.

translations.literal: Fire transmitted by the yang fire-drill; water irrigating the yin essence.
translations.idiomatic: Fire passes through the sun mirror; water nourishes the yin force within.

translations.literal: Taigong's half-tray offering; Yue's harmonized broth.
translations.idiomatic: Like Taigong at the offering stand, like Yue who perfected the broth.

translations.literal: Offering vessels are fragrant; the fast-day feast pure and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The stands and bowls are rich with scent; the sacred meal is clean and full.

translations.literal: There is also harmonized broth; already guarded, already balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonized broth is ready too; all is prepared and rightly ordered.

translations.literal: Drums, bells, pipes, and chime-stones; solemn singers harmonize and sound.
translations.idiomatic: Drums, bells, pipes, and stones ring; the solemn chorus sings as one.

translations.literal: Imperial, imperial is the royal ancestor; bestow upon us fulfillment of longing.
translations.idiomatic: Great and glorious is our forebear; grant us the fulfillment we long for.

sentences.zh: 皇帝酌醴齊用文舞一章：

translations.literal: For the emperor's libation of clear wine with civil dance, one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's libation of clear wine with the civil dance uses one part:

translations.literal: Sage counsels of nine virtues; true words five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ninefold sage wisdom; five thousand words of truth.

translations.literal: Blessings gather on the illustrious line; omens open the imperial forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune gathers on the royal house; signs mark the founders of the throne.

translations.literal: Lofty culture with battle-axe in hand; able to match that Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: With high virtue and axe of command, he is fit to match Heaven itself.

translations.literal: The three ancestors hold the mirror; the six directions shine brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Three forebears hold the mirror of rule; all six directions blaze with light.

translations.literal: The emperor shall continue the sacrifice; following ritual without fault.
translations.idiomatic: May the Son of Heaven keep the rite; may he follow every rule without error.

translations.literal: Maps and books emerge from mist; sun and moon hang clear.
translations.idiomatic: Charts and texts rise from the mist; sun and moon stand bright in the sky.

translations.literal: The dance embodies virtue's likeness; song praises and transmits merit.
translations.idiomatic: The dance shows virtue in form; the hymn sings and passes down their deeds.

translations.literal: Yellow dragons coil and writhe; colored clouds wheel and dance.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow dragons twist and turn; bright clouds swirl and drift.

translations.literal: The five phases' qi are harmonious; the eight rows spread the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The five elements flow in order; the eight ranks of dancers carry the breeze of rite.

translations.literal: May these hundred blessings be granted; may the Son of Heaven reign ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Grant a hundred blessings here; may the emperor reign ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 獻祖宣皇帝室奠獻用《光大》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Imperial Ancestor Emperor Xuan, use the dance "Guangda," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Imperial Ancestor Emperor Xuan uses the "Great Radiance" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn is the founding ancestor; vast, vast is the dredged source.
translations.idiomatic: Grave and glorious is our founding forebear; deep and wide is the stream he opened.

translations.literal: There was a heroic jade sword; it became the guardian of the Golden Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A jade sword of might became the ward of the Golden Gate.

translations.literal: The Dark King bequeathed the thread; Hou Ji planned for the descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Dark King left the line; Hou Ji laid plans for the generations.

translations.literal: He first established the nine temples; the four seas came to honor.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the nine shrines; all within the seas came to pay honor.

sentences.zh: 懿祖光皇帝室奠獻用《長髮》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Imperial Ancestor Emperor Guang, use the dance "Changfa," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Imperial Ancestor Emperor Guang uses the "Long Hair" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: Complete rites, exalt virtue; complete music, inherit the tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are full and virtue honored; music is prepared and the legacy upheld.

translations.literal: Wei pushed the banner lord; Zhou enfeoffed him as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wei urged the lord of the banner; Zhou granted him the rank of Minister of Works.

translations.literal: Without acting he arrived; without completing he had an end.
translations.idiomatic: Without striving he attained his goal; without finishing he reached fulfillment.

translations.literal: The spirits raised the royal enterprise; Heaven returned the imperial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The gods raised the royal cause; Heaven restored the throne's merit.

sentences.zh: 太祖景皇帝室奠獻用《大政》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Great Ancestor Emperor Jing, use the dance "Dazheng," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Great Ancestor Emperor Jing uses the "Great Governance" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: How majestic is the primal mandate; the chariot of imperial culture begins.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid is the first command; the imperial order begins to rise.

translations.literal: Heaven aligns the eight pillars; earth is half divided in three parts.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's eight pillars stand aligned; earth's realm is measured and set in order.

translations.literal: In the ancestral temple one observes virtue; sheng and yong music celebrate merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the temple we behold his virtue; bells and flutes praise his achievement.

translations.literal: The omen of enfeoffing Tang; becoming ruler of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The sign of Tang's enfeoffment came; he became sovereign of the world.

sentences.zh: 代祖元皇帝室奠獻用《大成》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Dynastic Ancestor Emperor Yuan, use the dance "Dacheng," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Dynastic Ancestor Emperor Yuan uses the "Great Completion" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: The emperor dances the Jili; inheriting the sage, he brings prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor performs the Jili dance; from the sage he inherits flourishing rule.

translations.literal: The empress's songs have Jiao; the womb carries fire and bears yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The queen's song brings Jiao; fire in the womb yields the Yellow Lord.

translations.literal: Heaven and earth combine in virtue; sun and moon share equal light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth join in virtue; sun and moon shine with one brightness.

translations.literal: Solemn and harmonious is the filial offering; may he bless our myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: In solemn grace we offer in filial rite; may he bless the lands under our rule.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝室奠獻用《大明》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao, use the dance "Daming," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao uses the "Great Brightness" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: The red essence lost virtue; the four seas were trapped in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui house lost the Way; the four seas languished in distress.

translations.literal: The yellow banner raised the righteous cause; the three numina joined as one.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow banner rose in righteous revolt; heaven, earth, and man united as one.

translations.literal: Long drought looked to spring rain; clouds parted before the great wind.
translations.idiomatic: As drought longed for spring rain, clouds broke before the mighty wind.

translations.literal: All under heaven come to the sacrifice; such is the High Ancestor's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The world gathers for the rite to honor the High Ancestor's deeds.

sentences.zh: 太宗文武聖皇帝室奠獻用《崇德》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Taizong, Wen and Wu, Sage Emperor, use the dance "Chongde," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Taizong, the Sage Emperor of Culture and Might, uses the "Exalted Virtue" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: The emperor unites in one virtue; the hundred spirits pay court.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven joins all in virtue; the hundred spirits bow in homage.

translations.literal: He cut down and pacified the realm; greatly saving the living people.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued the realm and brought peace; he rescued the people from ruin.

translations.literal: God on High shares the offering; the Xiongnu chieftain enters as subject.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven shares the feast; the northern khan submits as vassal.

translations.literal: Barbarian songs and arrayed dances; clamorous, resounding.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier songs and martial dances thunder in clamorous praise.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝室奠獻用《鈞天》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Gaozong, Heavenly Sovereign, use the dance "Juntian," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Gaozong, the Heavenly Sovereign, uses the "Harmonizing with Heaven" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: The high emperor advanced the Way; upright and folded hands, without action.
translations.idiomatic: The exalted emperor pursued the Way; he ruled at ease, doing nothing by force.

translations.literal: His transforming power embraced the Xiongnu tribes; weapons were stilled toward Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His grace reached the northern tribes; arms were laid down before Goguryeo.

translations.literal: Rites honored the feng and shan ceremonies; music flourished for the coming tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual exalted the feng and shan rites; music rose grandly for envoys from afar.

translations.literal: Combined in seat with the Empress of Nuwa; together styled Fuxi.
translations.idiomatic: They shared the throne like Fuxi and Nuwa; together they bore that sacred name.

sentences.zh: 中宗孝和皇帝室奠獻用《太和》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Zhongzong, Filial and Harmonious, use the dance "Taihe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Zhongzong, the Filial and Harmonious, uses the "Supreme Harmony" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: Retired to dwell by the River waters; lushly rose from Red Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the river's edge; from Crimson Hill he rose again in glory.

translations.literal: Rites and offerings restored to the old; court regulations centrally revived.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rites returned; the court's order was renewed at the center.

translations.literal: The dragon diagram's friends reach all; the majestic mandate reverently received.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings of the dragon emblem reach all; with reverence he received the exalted mandate.

translations.literal: Sounding the qiú, holding the guàn; the great millet-grain offering is received.
translations.idiomatic: He strikes the sounding-stone, grasps the libation cup, and receives the sacred grain.

sentences.zh: 睿宗大聖真皇帝室奠獻用《景雲》之舞一章：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Ruizong, Great Sage and True, use the dance "Jingyun," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Ruizong, the Great Sage and True Sovereign, uses the "Auspicious Clouds" dance, in one part:

translations.literal: Auspicious clouds luxuriant and bright; they announce to us the imperial tally.
translations.idiomatic: Bright auspicious clouds announce Heaven's sign to us.

translations.literal: Alas! the emperor's sublime virtue—he is Heaven's companion.
translations.idiomatic: How pure his virtue—he walks as Heaven's own companion.

translations.literal: Flutes and bells far distant; offering stands and vessels empty and void.
translations.idiomatic: Flutes and bells fade into the distance; the altars stand empty and still.

translations.literal: Spring and autumn, filial offerings; restored once again to this capital.
translations.idiomatic: Through the seasons we offer filial rites; the capital is restored once more.

translations.literal: Again: fourteen hymn pieces for offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen additional hymns for sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple

sentences.zh: 玄宗至道大聖大明孝皇帝室奠獻用《廣運》之舞一章司徒兼中書令、汾陽郡王郭子儀撰。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Xuanzong, Sagely Daoist Great Sage Bright Filial, use the dance "Guangyun," one sequence—composed by Minister of Works and concurrent Director of the Chancellery, Prince of Fenyang, Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Xuanzong, the Sagely Daoist Great Sage and Luminous Filial Sovereign, uses the "Expansive Fortune" dance, in one part—composed by Guo Ziyi, Minister of Works, Director of the Chancellery, and Prince of Fenyang.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: How brilliant the imperial forebear; bright illumination has harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Radiant is our royal founder; his bright virtue flows in harmony.

translations.literal: Only the virtue of culture; only the achievement of martial might.
translations.idiomatic: In civil virtue and martial glory alike he excels.

translations.literal: Rivers and seas quiet and still; chariots and writing unified as one.
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and seas lie still; chariots and script unite the realm.

translations.literal: Devoutly reverent in filial offerings; solemn, solemn, the dark wind.
translations.idiomatic: With devout reverence we offer filial rites; solemn is the sacred breeze.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝室奠獻用《惟新》之舞一章吏部尚書、平章事、彭城郡公劉晏撰。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Suzong, Civil and Martial Virtue Great Sage Great Proclamation Filial, use the dance "Weixin," one sequence—composed by Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Chief Minister, Duke of Pengcheng, Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Suzong, the Sagely Civil and Martial Proclaiming Filial Sovereign, uses the "Ever Renewed" dance, in one part—composed by Liu Yan, Director of Personnel, Chief Minister, and Duke of Pengcheng.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: The Han imperial fortune alone is eternal; divine achievement centrally revived.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial mandate endures forever; divine power restored the dynasty at its center.

translations.literal: Wind drives away miasma and vapors; Heaven covers the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: Wind scatters the miasma; Heaven shelters all the people.

translations.literal: The three luminaries again bright; the myriad achievements thereby coalesce.
translations.idiomatic: Sun, moon, and stars shine anew; all affairs gather in fulfillment.

translations.literal: Repeated glory, accumulated generations; the bright mandate is received.
translations.idiomatic: Glory layered through generations; he received the bright mandate.

sentences.zh: 皇帝飲福受脤用《福和》一章：

translations.literal: For the emperor drinking blessing and receiving sacrificial meat, use "Fuhe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor receives the blessing wine and sacrificial meat, the hymn is "Harmony of Blessings," in one part:

translations.literal: Complete the rites, employ music; exalt kin, governance honored.
translations.idiomatic: Rites complete, music raised; kin exalted, rule honored.

translations.literal: Sincerity penetrates, compassion descends; reverence withdrawn, love remains.
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity opens the way and grace descends; reverence endures and love lives on.

translations.literal: Offering with feeling, praising longevity; tasting and sensing, receiving grace.
translations.idiomatic: He offers with heartfelt praise for long life; tasting the sacrifice, he feels and receives grace.

translations.literal: The emperor's filial virtue—descendants by the thousand millions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's filial virtue brings descendants beyond count.

translations.literal: Greatly encompassing the celestial domain; long extending without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Great enough to embrace the heavens; enduring without end.

sentences.zh: 送文舞出、迎武舞入用《舒和》一章：

translations.literal: For sending out the civil dance and welcoming in the martial dance, use "Shuhe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: As the civil dance departs and the martial dance enters, the hymn is "Easy Harmony," in one part:

sentences.zh: 六鐘翕協六變成，八佾倘佯八風生。

translations.literal: Six bells harmoniously joined, six changes completed; eight rows of dancers wander leisurely, eight winds arise.
translations.idiomatic: Six bells blend till six changes complete; eight rows of dancers sway as the eight winds rise.

sentences.zh: 樂《九韶》兮人神感，美《七德》兮天地清。

translations.literal: Music of "Jiushao"—ah! men and spirits moved; beauty of "Qide"—ah! Heaven and Earth made clear.
translations.idiomatic: "Nine Shao" moves both human and divine; "Seven Virtues" clears Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻行事、武舞用《凱安》四章：

translations.literal: For the secondary offering, final offering rites, and martial dance, use "Kaian," four sequences:
translations.idiomatic: For the second and final offerings and the martial dance, four parts of "Triumphant Peace":

translations.literal: Majestic those jade cups; the secondary offering falls to the highest duke.
translations.idiomatic: Exalted are the jade goblets; the second offering is the highest duke's charge.

translations.literal: The chamber as if holding breath; the gate cannot contain the body.
translations.idiomatic: In the chamber all hold their breath; at the gate none may crowd the threshold.

translations.literal: Rites honor the root; music upholds the center.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual honors what lies at the root; music holds the mean.

translations.literal: The sage emperor eternally yearns; Heaven and Earth darkly communicate.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperor ever yearns; Heaven and Earth commune in mystery.

translations.literal: Rites complete three offerings; music spreads through nine accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Offerings circle thrice; music fills nine movements.

translations.literal: Descending along the hall steps; looking up sighing, the imperial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He descends the hall steps; looking up, his imperial heart sighs.

translations.literal: Blessing joins with benevolence; virtue through filial piety made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing joins with benevolence; virtue shines through filial devotion.

translations.literal: A hundred years, spirits in awe; the four seas, the wind's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred years the gods stand in awe; his influence rides the four seas like wind.

translations.literal: Gathered gathered shields and axes; resounding resounding drums and bells.
translations.idiomatic: Shields and axes mass together; drums and bells thunder without cease.

translations.literal: Exerting and raising, increasing spirit; sitting and acting as deportment.
translations.idiomatic: They rouse their spirits in vigor; sitting and rising form the ritual bearing.

translations.literal: Parting like fierce birds; joining like battling dragons.
translations.idiomatic: They scatter like hunting falcons; they unite like dragons at war.

translations.literal: Myriad regions observe the virtue; solemn, solemn, harmonious, harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm beholds his virtue; solemn and harmonious the scene.

sentences.zh: 烈祖順三靈，文宗威四海。

translations.literal: The blazing ancestor accorded with the three numina; the civil founder's majesty over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Our fierce founder obeyed Heaven, Earth, and Man; our civil sage awed the four seas.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞誅群盜，硃旗掃多罪。

translations.literal: Yellow battle-axes executed the band of robbers; vermilion banners swept away many crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Golden axes struck down the rebel hordes; crimson banners swept crimes away.

sentences.zh: 戢兵天下安，約法人心改。

translations.literal: Weapons stilled, the realm at peace; simplified laws, hearts of men transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Arms were laid down and the realm was at peace; tempered laws changed every heart.

sentences.zh: 大哉幹羽意，長見風雲在。

translations.literal: Great indeed the meaning of shields and feathers; long may one see wind and clouds present.
translations.idiomatic: How great the purpose of this civil dance; may wind and cloud ever remain!

translations.literal: For removing the bean vessels, ascending song, one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The ascending hymn for withdrawing the offerings, in one part:

translations.literal: Stop the pipes and chime-stones; remove the bean vessels and offering trays.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes and stones fall silent; the bean vessels and trays are withdrawn.

translations.literal: Vast without sound; distant, entering the dark mystery.
translations.idiomatic: All sound fades into silence; stillness sinks into mystery.

translations.literal: The lord is in the chamber; the spirit is in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign remains in the hall; the spirits return to Heaven.

translations.literal: Feeling surplus in yearning; rites without transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Devotion lingers in longing; no ritual fault remains.

translations.literal: Rejoicing in millet and grain; repeatedly abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: We rejoice in grain and millet; may harvests come year after year.

translations.literal: For sending off the spirits, use "Yonghe," one sequence:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn for escorting the spirits away is "Everlasting Harmony," in one part:

translations.literal: Dim and fine, the blessed music; entrusted to the numinous clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Faint and fair, the sacred music; entrusted to the spirits' bright presence.

translations.literal: Feeling as if they come; thought as if they go.
translations.idiomatic: Sensation says they have come; memory says they depart.

translations.literal: Restful qi disperses; returning wind ascends.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil breath disperses; the circling wind rises upward.

translations.literal: Returning to solitude; reverting to dim uncertainty.
translations.idiomatic: They return to silence; they fade into shadow and dream.

translations.literal: Cherishing the numinous chariot; gathering empty longing.
translations.idiomatic: We hold the spirits' departing carriage in mind; empty longing fills our hearts.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝室奠獻用《保大》之舞一章尚父郭子儀撰：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Daizong, Sage Culture Filial Martial, use the dance "Baoda," one sequence—composed by Supreme Preceptor Guo Ziyi:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Daizong, the Sage Civil and Filial Martial Sovereign, uses the "Preserving the Great" dance, in one part—composed by Guo Ziyi, Supreme Preceptor:

translations.literal: How solemn the civil forefather; sage spirit bright and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is our civil founder; sage and spirit, bright and clear.

translations.literal: "Xiao" and "Shao"—all wickedness; containing light, reaching far regions.
translations.idiomatic: With "Panpipe" and "Ladle" dances, all evil was quelled; his light reached the distant lands.

translations.literal: The ten thousand things flourish and succeed; the nine barbarians pay court to the king.
translations.idiomatic: All things flourish in turn; the nine tribes come as royal guests.

translations.literal: Gentle, gentle "Yun" and "Shao"; virtuous sounds not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Softly flows "Cloud" and "Shao"; his virtuous fame is never forgotten.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武孝文皇帝室奠獻用《文明》之舞一章尚書左丞平章事鄭餘慶撰：

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Dezong, Divine Martial Filial Culture, use the dance "Wenming," one sequence—composed by Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, Chief Minister, Zheng Yuqing:
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Dezong, the Divine Martial and Filial Civil Sovereign, uses the "Civil Brilliance" dance, in one part—composed by Zheng Yuqing, Left Assistant Director and Chief Minister:

translations.literal: Opening the residence, eliminating violence; the times advance, merit honored.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his domain and swept away tyranny; as time marched on, his merit was exalted.

translations.literal: The three origins announce the mandate; the four extremities gallop in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and Man proclaimed his mandate; the four quarters rushed to obey.

translations.literal: Golden branches, jade-green leaves; brilliance illuminates fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: Golden branches, emerald leaves—radiance shines on jade and gems.

translations.literal: Emblematic virtue for a hundred million years; bestowing felicity on Tang's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue endures ten thousand ages; blessings fall on Tang's heirs.

sentences.zh: 順宗至德大聖大安孝皇帝室奠獻用《大順》之舞一章中書侍郎、平章事鄭絪撰。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Shunzong, Supreme Virtue Great Sage Great Peace Filial, use the dance "Dashun," one sequence—composed by Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Minister, Zheng Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Shunzong, the Supreme Virtue Great Sage and Great Tranquil Filial Sovereign, uses the "Great Accord" dance, in one part—composed by Zheng Yin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: How solemn the timely culture; received Heaven's bright mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn is his cultured reign; he received Heaven's luminous command.

translations.literal: Truly reverent, darkly silent; transformation accomplished, order fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent and still in deep silence; his transforming rule set order firm.

translations.literal: Going forth from Zhen, succeeding in virtue; responding to Qian, transmitting sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the east with virtue; he answered Heaven and passed the sagehood on.

translations.literal: Ah! how continuous the bright glory; thousand millions flow with felicity.
translations.idiomatic: How bright and gathering his glory; blessings stream to endless heirs.

sentences.zh: 憲宗聖神章武孝皇帝室奠獻用《象德》之舞一章中書侍郎、平章事段文昌撰。

translations.literal: For the libation offering to the chamber of Emperor Xianzong, Sage Spirit Manifest Martial Filial, use the dance "Xiangde," one sequence—composed by Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Minister, Duan Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: The offering to Emperor Xianzong, the Sagely Spirit and Manifest Martial Filial Sovereign, uses the "Emblem of Virtue" dance, in one part—composed by Duan Wenchang, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.

translations.literal: Colon introducing the hymn text:
translations.idiomatic: The hymn reads:

translations.literal: Solemn, solemn, the pure temple; ascending to display utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn stands the pure temple; there we exalt supreme virtue.

translations.literal: Grace pervades the eight wilds; arms pacify the four extremities.
translations.idiomatic: His grace fills the eight directions; his armies secured the four corners.

translations.literal: Living things all succeed; bandits in masses extinguished and stilled.
translations.idiomatic: All living things flourish; rebel hordes are crushed and still.

translations.literal: Bright sage reverently receives; descendants thousand millions.
translations.idiomatic: The bright sage receives in reverence; his heirs will number beyond count.

translations.literal: Twelve hymn pieces for the Yikun Temple
translations.idiomatic: Twelve hymns for the Yikun Temple

sentences.zh: 迎神用《永和》林鐘宮，散騎常侍、昭文館學士徐彥伯作。

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirits, use "Yonghe," Linzhong palace mode—composed by Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalry, Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, Xu Yanbo.
